dispatch.headline: Eighty Miners Still Holding Drill
dispatch.body:
Efua Falconer bars the main drift with an iron strike-pad. Behind her, eighty miners have held a twenty-tonne bore-head three millimetres off the basalt floor since breakfast.

No cutter teeth may touch the rock until the memorial thud struck for surveyor Hemi finishes its forty-minute decay through the stone. The asteroid is dense. It rings like wet lead.

"The seam is still speaking," Falconer whispered, ear pressed to the rock rib. "He had sensitive ears."

Shift boss Wiremu Uchenna stood braced beneath a hydraulic arm, his knees shaking under seventy kilos of manual lift. Setting the steel down against stone would damp the tone, which shaft custom considers desecration.

At minute thirty-eight, driller Lior Silveira sneezed into his sleeve.

Falconer raised her hammer and struck the iron pad again.

The count restarted.

Uchenna did not swear. He merely leaned harder into the casing and signalled for two apprentices to take his left shoulder.

"Keep the teeth clear," Uchenna rasped through clenched teeth. "We do this right."

The crew has now suspended twenty tonnes on bare muscle for seven hours without cutting an ounce of ore. A relief shift just crept into the drift in woollen socks, carrying sandwiches nobody is allowed to chew.
dispatch.scene: A miner in a dust-caked harness strains under the crossbeam of a massive suspended rock-drill, two crewmen bracing his shoulders from behind in a narrow stone tunnel.

drafts.headline: Jettison Master Refuses To Fling Grandfather
drafts.body:
Lior Quintero blocked the memorial valve this morning, shouting at mourners that their grandfather deserved an arc instead of a ditch.

Beside the lock, Zygmunt Gallagher has spent five hours holding a chilled pod by its haul-straps. His arms were shaking. Inside the casing lies the late Ignacy Lukasiewicz, whose final crossing has been paused while Quintero refines the mathematics.

Quintero has redrawn the launch parabola forty times across the deck plates with a quartz stylus. Each draft aims to sweep Lukasiewicz past the sunrise shadow of Saturn without clipping incoming ore-tugs. None has satisfied Quintero.

"It is mere fly-tipping," Quintero shouted, wiping his brow with an oily cuff. "You would toss him out like rinds."

Gallagher begged for the release switch. The family had booked twelve minutes in the chamber, but Quintero refused to trip the vent until the curve possessed what he called proper weight.

He wiped the deck. He began again.

By midday, Quintero had factored in the drag from three passing bulk-haulers. The pod had moved four centimetres left. Lukasiewicz remains on the floor.
drafts.premise: An artisanal jettison-master at the Astraea freeport is refusing to open the memorial airlock, loudly berating a weeping family that launching their grandfather into space without calculating the visual poetry of his orbital ellipse is 'mere fly-tipping.'

drafts.headline: Widow Sobs All Shift Off Key
drafts.body:
Hemi Nieminen blocked the cold table with both elbows at dawn. Attendants were waiting to pull the dark rubber seal over a dead drill-captain, but Nieminen would not let the seam close.

Beside the trolley, Anouk Mirzoyan sat on an upturned air tank. She had spent seven hours sobbing into a brass funnel, trying to reach the Dorian mode.

Her throat was dry.

"The ascent is wrong," Nieminen said, gently kneading Mirzoyan's diaphragm to reset her lung rhythm. "You are weeping in the major scale. That is for harvest domes."

Mirzoyan swallowed a cup of warm salt water, adjusted her knees, and began another descent. Mortuary attendant Tavita Esposito waited with two heavy straps held tight against the table edge. Esposito had lowered the winch four centimetres since breakfast.

"She hits the proper third when she remembers his shaft accidents," Esposito said. "Then she thinks of his voice and sharpens."

By mid-afternoon, Nieminen had guided Mirzoyan through eighty-four attempts. She had produced four pure notes and swallowed three litres of salt water. Esposito had lowered the winch another centimetre. The corpse remained waist-high.
drafts.premise: A certified vacuum-lamenter at the Ceres deep-shaft morgue has physically blocked mortuary attendants from bagging a dead drill-captain, demanding the widow restart her sobs because her grief drifted out of the historically certified Dorian mode.

drafts.headline: Mason Halts Repair To Beat Ash
drafts.body:
Akosua Mwangi knelt beside the split rock face this morning, beating a tub of grey bone foam with two flat paddles. Behind her, the south wall of the main nickel drift groaned and threw thirty tonnes of gravel onto the haul track. Mwangi did not look up. She has spent nine hours whisking the powdered remains of shift foreman Ilse Sandoval into twenty litres of warm binder slag, aiming for a firm foam before pumping it into the split.

"If it goes in flat, Ilse sinks to the floor plates," Mwangi said, wiping grey froth from her forearms. "A foreman belongs through the seam. Not down by the boots."

Four junior sealers have taken turns on the paddles since midnight. The foam collapsed three times when the gallery chilled.

Rock mechanic Luana Bakshi measured the widening split with an optical rod every ten minutes. The gap has grown from two centimetres to half a metre. Air whistles through to the void.

"They are working very hard," Bakshi said, retreating three steps as the ceiling shed another shower of iron grit. "The texture is improving."

Mwangi called for fresh binder. The crack lengthened.
drafts.premise: Emergency reinforcement of a cracking gallery on Asteroid 16 Psyche has ground to a halt because a master slag-incorporator refuses to seal the fissure until a deceased shift foreman’s bone-ash is whipped to the guild-mandated artisanal density.

drafts.headline: Miners Hold Up Drill For Funeral Thud
drafts.body:
Efua Falconer bars the main drift with an iron strike-pad. Behind her, eighty miners have held a twenty-tonne bore-head three millimetres off the basalt floor since noon.

No industrial teeth may touch the stone until the memorial thud struck for a surveyor finishes its forty-minute decay through the rock. The asteroid is dense. It rings like wet lead.

"The seam is still speaking," Falconer said, ear pressed to the shaft rib.

Shift boss Wiremu Uchenna stood braced beneath a hydraulic arm, his forearms trembling under sixty kilos of manual tension. He has forbidden the crew to set the cutter down because resting metal against stone dampens the tone. Nobody moved.

At minute thirty-nine, driller Lior Silveira sneezed into his glove.

Falconer raised her mallet and hit the strike-pad again.

The count restarted.

Uchenna merely adjusted his stance and signalled for two more lifters to take his right shoulder.

"We honour the surveyor," Uchenna whispered, his teeth grinding with effort.

The crew has now held the rig suspended for six hours without cutting a gram of ore. A relief shift just entered the tunnel barefoot.

quality.judge_reason: Superb escalation with the minute-39 sneeze reset and the barefoot relief shift kicker.
quality.critique:
The headline was descriptive rather than funny, missing the mounting physical agony of the crew.
The original ending petered out without exploiting the absurd acoustic rule the miners had committed to.

picture.reason: It fails to depict the rock-drill's crossbeam, showing a man holding thin suspension cables instead.
picture.winner_faults: Only two miners are present instead of three, and no crewmen are bracing the main miner's shoulders.
